title: When Imperfect Automated Fact-Checking Backfires: Social Learning in the Presence of Misinformation
title_zh: 《当不完美的事实核查工具产生反效果时：错误信息存在下的社会学习》

paragraphs.en: Automated fact-checking tools, cheap and fast but imperfect, are increasingly available on social platforms. We study when such tools can backfire in a sequential social learning model of misinformation. Agents observe an article’s reliability and their predecessors’ actions, which indicate whether they liked or disliked the article. They may also pay to fact-check it. We examine how welfare, defined as the probability of a correct cascade, changes when a free, error-prone automated tool supplements costly but perfectly accurate manual fact-checking. Two opposing effects arise. Broader use of fact-checking helps agents escape wrong cascades. At the same time, errors from the automated tool can mislead agents who would otherwise have verified the article perfectly, reducing the likelihood of correct cascades. We prove that adding the tool strictly lowers welfare for articles of intermediate reliability when truthful articles are not too informative and manual checking is sufficiently costly. Simulations show that the tool can help on either side of the intermediate range, and that it improves on manual-only checking on average only above a threshold accuracy.

paragraphs.en: “Try AI companion”, “ask anything”—social platforms increasingly invite users to talk to AI assistants built into their interfaces [ 1 ] , and many users already turn to them as fact-checking tools [ 2 , 3 , 4 ] . Such tools are quick and easy to use, but imperfect: their accuracy differs between true and false claims [ 5 ] , and they can even reduce users’ ability to tell the two apart [ 6 ] . When a user consults a tool privately, others see only what she does, not what the tool told her, so a mistaken check can spread through actions and shape what a community comes to believe. This poses a design question for platforms: when does offering such a tool help collective learning, and when does it hurt?

paragraphs.en: This is a social learning question. Sequential social learning models have long been studied by economists [ 7 , 8 , 9 , 10 ] , and are also used to study online misinformation spread and fact-checking [ 11 , 12 ] . In such models, typically, Bayesian agents sequentially make decisions based on their private signals and the observed actions of their predecessors. A key feature of these models is that, under appropriate conditions, an information cascade occurs when agents follow others’ actions and ignore their private information. In this case, not only does social learning stop, but agents could also herd on the wrong action, that is, a wrong cascade can arise.
paragraphs.zh: 这是一个社会学习问题。 序贯社会学习模型长期以来一直被经济学家研究 [ 7 , 8 , 9 , 10 ] ，也被用于研究线上错误信息传播和事实核查 [ 11 , 12 ] 。 在这类模型中，典型情况下，贝叶斯智能体基于其私有信号以及观察到的前序智能体的行动依次做出决策。 这些模型的一个关键特征是，在适当条件下，当智能体跟随他人的行动并忽视自己的私有信息时，会发生信息级联。 在这种情况下，不仅社会学习会停止，智能体还可能在错误的行动上从众，也就是说，可能出现错误的级联。

paragraphs.en: In this paper, we study misinformation spread and fact-checking through a sequential social learning model. Agents arrive one after another and each likes or dislikes the same news article. They are uncertain about its veracity, which determines their payoff, but they know its reliability, the prior probability that it is truthful, and observe the actions of their predecessors. Before acting, an agent may fact-check the article. The check returns a private signal about the veracity, may be costly, and is subject to two-sided error rates. This differs from [ 11 ] and [ 13 ] , where fact-checking is public, and from [ 12 ] , where it is perfectly accurate. Our setting covers the situation where users fact-check privately, so a check informs others only through the action it leads to.
paragraphs.zh: 在本文中，我们通过一个序贯社会学习模型来研究错误信息的传播与事实核查。 智能体接连到来，每人都对同一篇新闻文章表示喜欢或不喜欢。 智能体不确定该文章的真实性（真实性决定其收益），但智能体知道其可靠性，即它为真的先验概率，并且能观察到前人的行动。 在行动之前，智能体可以对文章进行事实核查。 核查会返回一个关于真实性的私人信号，可能需要付出成本，并且存在两类错误率。 这与 [11] 和 [13] 不同，在那里事实核查是公开的；也与 [12] 不同，在那里核查是完全准确的。 我们的设定涵盖了用户私下进行事实核查的情形，因此核查只能通过它所导致的行动来告知他人。

paragraphs.en: We focus on two idealized fact-checking methods. Manual fact-checking is a costly investigation that takes time and effort, but is error-free, as in [ 12 ] . Automated fact-checking , such as asking an AI assistant, is free and easy to use but has two-sided error rates, so it can mislead. Idealizing manual fact-checking as error-free gives a clean baseline that isolates the effect of the automated tool’s errors. We study how welfare , defined as the probability of a correct cascade, changes when the automated tool is added alongside manual fact-checking, as when a platform builds it into its interface.
paragraphs.zh: 我们关注两种理想化的事实核查方法。 人工事实核查是一项耗时费力的高成本调查，但不会出错，如 [ 12 ] 所示。 自动化事实核查，例如询问 AI 助手，免费且易于使用，但存在双向错误率，因此可能产生误导。 将人工事实核查理想化为无错误，提供了一个干净的基线，从而分离出自动化工具自身错误的影响。 我们研究当在人工事实核查之外加入自动化工具时（例如平台将其集成到界面中），定义为正确级联概率的福利如何变化。

paragraphs.en: The main contributions of the paper are as follows. We characterize when correct and wrong cascades arise with positive probability, via thresholds on the article’s reliability that are explicit in the cost and error rates of the fact-checking method. We prove that adding the automated tool strictly decreases welfare for articles of reliability within an intermediate range, when manual fact-checking is sufficiently costly and truthful articles are not too informative, since the tool’s errors can start wrong cascades that manual checking would have avoided. Simulations show that welfare can also increase on both sides of this range if every agent who checks prefers the tool, and on one side if it replaces manual checking for only some agents. A further simulation varies the accuracy of the tool, showing that welfare falls once agents start to use it and exceeds the manual-only baseline only above a threshold accuracy, suggesting that a platform should not offer the tool below that accuracy.

paragraphs.en: Proposition 2 shows two opposing effects of switching from ℳ H {{\cal M}_{\mathrm{H}}} to ℳ A {{\cal M}_{\mathrm{A}}} . The first is broader checking : since ℳ A {{\cal M}_{\mathrm{A}}} is free and accurate enough, agents check over a wider range of posteriors (Fig. 2(b) ). A truthful article of moderately low reliability, which every agent dislikes without checking under ℳ H {{\cal M}_{\mathrm{H}}} , is now checked by some agents and escapes this wrong cascade with positive probability. So does a fake article of moderately high reliability. These are the positive bands in Figs. 3(a) and 3(b) .
paragraphs.zh: 命题2展示了从 ℳ H {{\cal M}_{\mathrm{H}}} 切换到 ℳ A {{\cal M}_{\mathrm{A}}} 所带来的两种相反效应。 第一种效应是更广泛的核查：由于 ℳ A {{\cal M}_{\mathrm{A}}} 是免费且足够准确的，智能体会在更宽的后验范围内进行核查（图2(b)）。 一篇可靠性中等偏低的真实文章，在 ℳ H {{\cal M}_{\mathrm{H}}} 下每个智能体不经核查就会不喜欢它，而现在会被一些智能体核查，并以正概率逃脱这种错误级联。 可靠性中等偏高的虚假文章也是如此。 这些就是图3(a)和图3(b)中的正区间。

paragraphs.en: This paper studied how a free, error-prone automated fact-checking tool changes the probability of a correct cascade when it is offered alongside costly but accurate manual fact-checking. The tool helps agents escape wrong cascades by bringing more of them to check, but its errors, passed on through their actions, can start wrong cascades that manual checking would have avoided. The second effect dominates for articles of intermediate reliability, and on average over articles the tool raises welfare only if it is accurate enough. A platform should therefore not offer such a tool before its accuracy exceeds a threshold. Several questions remain for future research. First, we found the accuracy threshold above which the tool raises average welfare by simulation, but characterizing it analytically would say how accurate a tool must be before it helps. Second, a tool of given ability can trade one error rate against the other: which operating point maximizes welfare? Third, with more than two channels of information with different costs and accuracies, which should a platform make available?
